## 1. The grain with seven spikes  (`#the-grain-and-its-spikes`)

Cited ayat: 2:261

> **2:261** مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنۢبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِى كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةٍ مِّا۟ئَةُ حَبَّةٍ وَٱللَّهُ يُضَٰعِفُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (2:261): The ayah gives a similitude: those who spend their wealth in the way of God are like a grain that grew seven spikes, with a hundred grains in each spike.

**c2** (2:261): The ayah adds that God multiplies for whom He wills, and that God is vast and knowing.

### One-minute summary

The ayah likens those who spend their wealth in the way of God to a grain that grew seven spikes, with a hundred grains in each spike [c1]. It adds that God multiplies for whom He wills [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah gives a similitude [c1]. Those who spend their wealth in the way of God are like a grain that grew seven spikes, and in each spike there is a hundred grains [c1]. The ayah adds that God multiplies for whom He wills, and that God is vast and knowing [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah names what is likened (spending wealth in the way of God) and what it is likened to (a grain and its growth) [c1]. It states the figures as part of the similitude and then says separately that God multiplies for whom He wills [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah says that spending wealth in the way of God is like a grain that grows seven spikes [c1]. In each spike there are a hundred grains [c1]. God gives more to whom He wills [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the similitude presents spending in the way of God as growth, as a single grain grows into many [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah closes by saying that God is vast and knowing [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the ayah counts as spending in the way of God beyond its own words, or when and how the multiplying takes place.
- Not established: whether the figures in the similitude are to be read as exact quantities or as a picture of growth.
- The ayah itself calls the passage a similitude (mathal).
- The Arabic word sunbula is rendered 'spike' in this draft; a scholar may prefer another word for the part of the plant that holds the grains.
